summary: rfind returns the starting index of the last matching substring.
documentation: rfind returns the starting index of the last matching substring. A missing substring returns -1, and an empty substring matches at the end. It reports a position without changing the string or reversing its characters.
inputs: An object with text and needle strings.
caution: The returned index is in the original string. A result of zero is a successful match, so do not treat truthiness as a presence check.
scenarios: Find the final separator in an imported path-like label.
Locate the last marker in a local diagnostic line.
Identify the trailing occurrence of a repeated token in a preview.
title: Locate the final substring
problem: Input is {text, needle}. Return the start index of the last occurrence of needle, or -1 when missing. An empty needle returns len(text).
goal: Use str.rfind() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
